findings.where: Nav wordmark ("MantaHostels home"), nav "Destinations", and the footer links "Privacy", "Terms" and "Report content"
findings.fault: These links look like they lead somewhere else, but they don't. The wordmark, Privacy, Terms and Report content all go back to this same page. Destinations points to #destinations, and this page has no destinations section, so nothing happens.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who taps the logo to get home, or Destinations to start looking for a hostel, ends up where they started. Someone who wants the privacy terms, or wants to report a review, can't get to them. On a page whose whole job is trust, a dead "Report content" link makes Manta look like it hides the route for complaints.

findings.where: The heading and lede ("how a hostel's position is decided") against the Ranking method section
findings.fault: The page promises to say how a hostel's position is decided, but never says what orders the list. It says what rank does not depend on (payment, review count as the default sort). The only positive answer is "the reviews and information on record". It never says whether the default order is the score, something else, or a mix.
findings.who_objects: A sceptical traveller comes here to check why one hostel sits above another, and leaves without the answer. The founder's principle that "rankings and scoring methods are published" is only half kept.

findings.where: "Hostelworld, for comparison" section, the last section on the page
findings.fault: The page names a competitor and ends on a negative point about how its scores work ("a hostel with a small recent base can look thin there"). PRODUCT.md says the demand-side message names no competitor and never competes with Hostelworld. The Hostelworld affiliate application is still pending.
findings.who_objects: The founder: this goes against the positioning and risks the pending Hostelworld relationship. A traveller reads the page's ending as a dig at a rival, which makes it feel like a pitch instead of an honest method.

findings.where: Ranking method, third paragraph ("our approval checks decide whether a review earns its writer a reward")
findings.fault: The page lets slip, in passing, that reviewers are rewarded. It never explains the reward, or why a rewarded review isn't biased toward praise. Incentives are the main objection to the scores, and the page raises it without answering it.
findings.who_objects: A traveller deciding whether to trust Manta's scores reads "earns its writer a reward" and suspects paid-for praise. The page meant to build trust plants that doubt.

findings.where: Ranking method and Scoring method sections; the word scale
findings.fault: The section headings don't sort the content. Ranking method holds most of the scoring rules: pulling thin scores toward the area average, which reviews count, badges and "No reviews yet". Scoring method holds only the time decay. The page also never explains the words Loved, Great, Solid and Mixed that sit beside every score.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who jumps to "Scoring method" to find out what a score or a "Great" means misses most of the answer, which sits under the other heading.

findings.where: First screen: the lede, the summary paragraph and the three-item list, then repeated in the sections
findings.fault: The same points come up three times. The summary paragraph says them, the numbered list says them again, and the sections open by saying them a third time ("No hostel can pay for a higher position" word for word). Meanwhile the strongest claim, that no hostel can pay for rank, gets only list-item body type, the same weight as the other two points.
findings.who_objects: A phone reader scrolls past repeats, and the one promise they came to check doesn't stand out as the page's headline claim.

findings.where: Ranking method paragraphs two to four, worst on the phone (13 to 15 lines each)
findings.fault: The rules are buried in long, unbroken paragraphs. No term or number is pulled out, so the page can't be skimmed.
findings.who_objects: The primary user reads on a phone, mid-trip, and skims. They won't dig through a 15-line paragraph to find out whether a few reviews can sink a hostel.

findings.where: Whole page, no date or version anywhere
findings.fault: The method has no "last updated" date or version, so a reader can't tell whether it is current, or whether it changed since they last looked.
findings.who_objects: A visitor checking a published method needs to know it is the one in force now. Without a date, "we publish the method" can't be checked.

findings.fault: The page is a bare text column on sand with no brand moment. There is no illustration and no stated claim, and the right half of the screen is empty. It reads as an unstyled policy document.
findings.who_objects: The founder: the brand sheet names sterile or corporate as the enemy and asks for a loud claim with calm mechanics beneath it. This page has only the calm half.

findings.where: The two numbered lists (the summary list and the decay list)
findings.fault: The summary points are set as a numbered 1-2-3 list, which suggests a sequence or a priority they don't have.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader may take "1" as the most important factor in ranking, which the page doesn't mean.
